chapterNote: The psalm of 'only' — the Hebrew particle ak, 'alone, only, surely,' opens six of its twelve verses like a tolling bell, and the whole psalm is an exercise in subtraction until one thing is left. In God ALONE my soul is silent; He ALONE is my rock and my salvation. David is under assault by men who mean to topple him like a leaning wall, who bless with their mouths and curse in their hearts — and his response is not counterattack but a silence that waits. The center of the psalm turns from self to congregation: trust in Him at all times, you people; pour out your heart before Him; God is a refuge for us. Then the scales come out: the lowborn are a breath, the highborn a lie, and weighed together they rise lighter than vapor — so do not lean on extortion, do not set your heart on riches that grow. The close is the psalm's creed, learned by repetition: once God has spoken, twice I have heard it — power belongs to God, and covenant love belongs to You, O Lord, for You repay every man according to his work. Strength and mercy in the same hands; that is why silence before Him is safe.

1.text: For the choir director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of David. Only toward God is my soul silent and still; from Him comes my salvation.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], to Jeduthun [Yeduthun], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Truly ['Only', ak, the KJV margin] my soul waits ['is silent', dumiyyah, the KJV margin] upon God [Elohim]: from Him comes my salvation [yeshuah].
1.notes: The first ak, 'only' — the psalm's tolling word. dumiyyah (H1747) is stillness, the soul gone quiet the way a child does on its mother's shoulder (cf. Psalm 131:2): not resignation but the calm of a settled address. Jeduthun (H3038) was David's chief musician (cf. 1 Chronicles 16:41).

2.text: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my high stronghold; I will not be greatly shaken.
2.amp: He only [ak] is my rock [tsur] and my salvation [yeshuah]; He is my defence ['high place', misgab, the KJV margin — secure height]; I shall not be greatly [rav] moved [mot].
2.notes: Three titles under one 'only': tsur, yeshuah, misgab (H6697, H3444, H4869) — rock, rescue, and the unscalable height of Psalm 46. The honesty is in 'greatly': lo emmot rabbah — not 'never shaken' but not shaken MUCH; by verse 6 the qualifier will fall away.

3.text: How long will all of you keep battering a man, to murder him, all of you together — as if he were a leaning wall, a fence about to fall?
3.amp: How long will ye imagine mischief [hathath — assault, batter] against a man [ish]? ye shall be slain [ratsach — murdered] all of you: as a bowing [natah — leaning] wall [qir] shall ye be, and as a tottering [dachah — pushed-over] fence [gader].
3.notes: The enemies' picture of David: a qir natui (H7023, H5186), a wall already leaning, that one more shove (dachah, H1760) will drop — and they all push together. ratsach (H7523) is the murder-verb of the sixth commandment: their intent named at its true weight.

4.text: They plot only to topple him from his high place; they delight in the lie. With their mouth they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah.
4.amp: They only [ak] consult [yaats] to cast him down [nadach — thrust him out] from his excellency [seeth — his elevation]: they delight [ratsah] in lies [kazab]: they bless [barak] with their mouth [peh], but they curse [qalal] inwardly ['in their inward parts', qereb, the KJV margin]. Selah [selah].
4.notes: The enemies get an 'only' of their own: ak — their whole counsel (yaats, H3289) is one item, demotion. ratsah be-kazab (H7521, H3577): they take pleasure in the lie itself. The split man of James 3:10 in the Psalter — barak on the peh, qalal in the qereb.

5.text: Only toward God, O my soul, be silent and still, for my hope comes from Him.
5.amp: My soul [nephesh], wait [damam — be silent, be still] you only [ak] upon God [Elohim]; for my expectation [tiqvah — my hope, my cord] is from Him.
5.notes: Verse 1 as testimony becomes verse 5 as command: David talks to his nephesh, damam (H1826) — be still — as Psalm 42's self-preaching. tiqvah (H8615) is hope built on the word for a cord: the line that held Rahab's window (cf. Joshua 2:18), expectation as a rope anchored elsewhere.

6.text: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my high stronghold; I will not be shaken.
6.amp: He only [ak] is my rock [tsur] and my salvation [yeshuah]: He is my defence [misgab]; I shall not be moved [mot].
6.notes: The refrain of verse 2 returns with one word gone: 'greatly' has been dropped. Between the two verses the soul was ordered still (v. 5), and the qualifier fell away — lo emmot, I will not be shaken, full stop. Repetition in this psalm is progress.

7.text: On God rests my salvation and my glory; the rock of my strength, my refuge, is in God.
7.amp: In God [Elohim] is my salvation [yesha] and my glory [kabod]: the rock [tsur] of my strength [oz], and my refuge [machseh], is in God.
7.notes: The inventory doubled: yesha and kabod (H3468, H3519), rescue and honor — the very seeth (v. 4) the enemies plotted to strip — filed under God's name. tsur oz and machseh (H5797, H4268): the rock to stand on and the shelter to run to, both be-Elohim.

8.text: Trust in Him at every moment, you people; pour out your heart before Him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
8.amp: Trust [batach] in Him at all times [et]; ye people [am], pour out [shaphak] your heart [lebab] before [panim] Him: God [Elohim] is a refuge [machseh] for us. Selah.
8.notes: The psalm turns from 'my' to 'us': David's private silence becomes public counsel. shaphak lebab (H8210, H3824), the heart poured out like water — Hannah's verb (cf. 1 Samuel 1:15) — be-kol-et, in every season. Stillness before God (v. 5) and outpouring to Him (v. 8) are the same trust in two postures.

9.text: Surely the sons of the lowly are a breath, and the sons of the mighty a lie; laid on the scales they rise, together lighter than a breath.
9.amp: Surely [ak] men of low degree [bene adam] are vanity [hebel — a breath], and men of high degree [bene ish] are a lie [kazab]: to be laid [alah — go up] in the balance [moznayim], they are altogether ['alike', yachad, the KJV margin] lighter than vanity [hebel].
9.notes: The scales-verse: bene adam, the commoners, weigh hebel (H1892), Ecclesiastes' vapor; bene ish, the nobility, weigh kazab — a lie, a promise that cannot pay. Put on the moznayim (H3976) they alah, they RISE, the pan lifting as it does when nothing is in it. All human trust-objects, audited: lighter than breath.

10.text: Do not put your trust in extortion, and do not set empty hopes on robbery; if riches bear fruit, do not set your heart upon them.
10.amp: Trust [batach] not in oppression [osheq — extortion], and become not vain [habal — vaporous] in robbery [gazel]: if riches [chayil] increase [nub — bear fruit, flourish], set [shith] not your heart [leb] upon them.
10.notes: Three false refuges: osheq (H6233) and gazel, wealth by force and theft, and honest chayil (H2428) that nub (H5107), grows like fruit on a tree. The last is the subtle one — prosperity itself is permitted; the heart shith (H7896), set upon it, is the idolatry (cf. 1 Timothy 6:17).

11.text: Once God has spoken; twice I have heard it: that strength belongs to God.
11.amp: God [Elohim] has spoken [dabar] once [echad]; twice [shenayim] have I heard [shama] this; that power ['strength', oz, the KJV margin] belongs unto God [Elohim].
11.notes: The Hebrew idiom of confirmed certainty — said once, heard twice (cf. Job 33:14): a truth God stated and the listener kept receiving. The content is the psalm's foundation: ki oz le-Elohim (H5797) — strength is His property, which is why the leaning wall (v. 3) is not actually falling.

12.text: And to You, O Lord, belongs covenant love, for You repay every man according to his work.
12.amp: Also unto You, O Lord [Adonai], belongs mercy [chesed — covenant love]: for You render [shalam — repay, complete] to every man [ish] according to his work [maaseh].
12.notes: The second thing heard: oz (v. 11) and chesed (H2617) in the same hands — power without love would be terror, love without power would be sentiment; God is neither. shalam (H7999) le-ish ke-maasehu: the just repayment that makes silence before Him safe for the wronged and sobering for the wall-pushers (cf. Romans 2:6; Matthew 16:27).
